issues.legal_issue: An unoverruled Supreme Court rule governing capital sentencing binds courts deciding whether to impose or uphold a death sentence.
material_facts: The appeal concerned death sentences imposed for murder and confirmed by the High Court.
The Court considered the rules stated in earlier Supreme Court decisions on sentencing for murder and held that they had not been overruled by a larger bench.
issues.conclusion: The sentencing rules laid down in the earlier Supreme Court decisions were binding under Article 141 and had to be applied by the courts below.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 141 of the Constitution, the law declared by the Supreme Court binds courts. The Court treated the sentencing principles in Ediga Annamma v State of Andhra Pradesh, Rajendra Prasad v State of Uttar Pradesh, and Bishnu Deo Shaw v State of West Bengal as governing law until overruled by a larger bench.

predicates.capital_sentencing_proceeding: A court is deciding whether to impose, confirm, or review a sentence of death for murder.
predicates.supreme_court_sentencing_rule_unoverrule: The Supreme Court has stated a rule governing capital sentencing, and a larger bench has not overruled it.
predicates.lower_courts_bound_by_sentencing_rule: Courts deciding the case must apply the governing Supreme Court sentencing rule.

issues.definition: When a court is deciding a capital sentence and an applicable Supreme Court sentencing rule remains unoverruled, the courts deciding the case must apply that rule.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence requires special reasons that take account of the offender, and the gravity or number of deaths alone does not justify the extreme penalty.
material_facts: The High Court affirmed death sentences after emphasizing that the two accused had fired at and killed three unarmed people.
The Supreme Court considered that sentencing factors had been dealt with casually, as though the nature of the crime alone determined punishment.
issues.conclusion: The court imposing a death sentence must record special reasons, and sentencing must consider the offender and the offender’s circumstances rather than focus solely on the crime or the number of victims.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 302 of the Indian Penal Code and 354(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provide the choice between death and life imprisonment and require special reasons for death. Section 235(2) CrPC provides for a sentencing hearing. Applying Ediga Annamma, Rajendra Prasad, and Bishnu Deo Shaw, the Court held that sentencing must consider the criminal and the offender’s social and personal circumstances; the crime’s gravity or the number of deaths is not by itself the controlling criterion.

predicates.death_sentence_case: A court is deciding whether a person convicted of murder should receive a death sentence.
predicates.sentencing_based_only_on_crime: The sentencing court focuses on the nature or number of the crimes and does not adequately consider the offender and the offender’s circumstances.
predicates.death_sentence_not_justified_without_spe: A death sentence is not justified without special reasons that take account of the offender.

issues.definition: If a court deciding a death sentence focuses only on the crime and inadequately considers the offender, the death sentence is not justified without special offender-related reasons.

issues.legal_issue: Death sentences are not warranted where the circumstances include provocation by the deceased’s side, intoxication, an antecedent dispute, and no well-planned attack aimed at eliminating the opposing group.
material_facts: An irrigation-water dispute between the groups had been addressed by mediation but remained a source of friction.
Members of the prosecution group were drinking when one appellant arrived and was beaten by them.
The appellant later returned with armed companions and the attack resulted in three deaths.

The Supreme Court found that the deceased’s side had supplied the earlier provocation, that the parties were tipsy, that the dispute predated the incident, and that there had been no pre-planned, well-laid attack to eliminate the opposing group.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences were reduced to life imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 IPC and 354(3) CrPC, death is the graver alternative and requires special reasons. Applying the offender-focused sentencing principles in Ediga Annamma, Rajendra Prasad, and Bishnu Deo Shaw, the majority held that the circumstances of provocation, intoxication, antecedent dispute, and absence of a planned attack did not warrant death.

rule.if: appeal_against_death_sentence and provocation_by_deceased_side and participants_tipsy and antecedent_dispute and no_well_planned_attack

predicates.appeal_against_death_sentence: A convicted person appeals against a death sentence for murder.
predicates.provocation_by_deceased_side: Members of the deceased’s side first provoked the confrontation by beating the accused.
predicates.participants_tipsy: The people involved in the confrontation, including members of the prosecution group, had been drinking.
predicates.antecedent_dispute: The groups had a pre-existing dispute that remained unresolved despite mediation.
predicates.no_well_planned_attack: The attack was not a pre-planned, well-laid effort to eliminate the opposing group.
predicates.death_sentence_reduced_to_life_imprisonm: The death sentence is replaced with a sentence of life imprisonment.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a death sentence involves provocation by the deceased’s side, intoxicated participants, an antecedent dispute, and no well-planned attack, the death sentence is reduced to life imprisonment.
